name: High and critical alerts to case (any source)
description: For every ingested alert with severity critical or high: promote it into a case grouped by source and title (one open case per source and title within 24 h), tagged with the source.
setup:
Works with any source: the cloud and SaaS pulls (`aws-guardduty`, `aws-securityhub`, `ms-sentinel`, `wiz`, `proofpoint-tap`, `github`), webhooks and the other vendor templates.

## Rules
- Trigger filter `alert.severity in ['critical', 'high']`: medium, low and info alerts stay pending in the Alerts queue.
- `alert_promote` mode `group`, key `source:<source>:<title>` (title cut to 200 characters), window 24 h: repeats of the same finding or rule land in one open case; a different title or source opens a new case. The case gets the alert's severity and title and the tag `<source>`.

## Narrowing
Edit the workflow's trigger filter, for example:
- only some sources: `alert.severity in ['critical', 'high'] and alert.source in ['aws-guardduty', 'wiz']`
- leave sources that have their own triage template alone: `alert.severity in ['critical', 'high'] and alert.source not in ['crowdstrike', 'sentinelone', 'okta', 'm365-defender', 'entra-id']`
- critical only: `alert.severity == 'critical'`

Two triage workflows matching the same alert race: the second promote finds the alert no longer pending and that run fails. Keep the filters disjoint.

To group per entity instead (for example per AWS account), change `group_key`, e.g. `source:{{ alert.source }}:{{ alert.payload.get('accountId') or alert.payload.get('AwsAccountId') or alert.title }}`.
